prompt: Silhouette: Four-legged brown bear frame. Host frame: the brown bear sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines a european rhinoceros beetle and a brown bear. Head of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: brown bear body and legs, with its own dense fur everywhere else, plain coat, no stripes or spots; from the european rhinoceros beetle, as parts and materials on the brown bear's own body: a single curved horn of hard, glossy chitin rising from the brow; a covering of hard, glossy chitin plates with fine seams in its own colors that replaces the brown bear's fur over the back and flanks: it grows in the skin as the brown bear's own covering there, not as pieces added on top; the fur stops at the covering's edge, and the belly and legs keep the brown bear's own fur; the covering is a carapace grown in the skin like an armadillo's, shaped like a beetle's two elytra: one domed dorsal shield from the shoulders to the hips, in two halves meeting at a midline seam, never scattered plates; anatomical anchors: the horn is rooted on the nasal bone like a rhinoceros horn, its base merging into the skin of the snout and brow; the shield is anchored along the spine. The covering follows the body outline. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and visible breathing openings along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.

spark_open.description: The creature is a quadrupedal mammal shown in right-facing profile with the overall size, proportions, shaggy fur, head shape, paws and claws of a brown bear, but with a single long curved horn on its forehead and a large glossy dark brown shell covering most of its dorsal side from behind the neck to above the hindquarters. The body is covered in dense long brown fur that is lighter cream-tan on the muzzle, chest and underside, standing on four thick legs with a short stubby tail at the rear, while the shell is domed, heavily ridged and divided into two main sections that sit on top of the fur.
